lessons.title: The parts of a computer
lessons.html:
Computers in agri business

Computers are used in every agri business: the co-op till system, stock control, accounts, grain intake at the silo, feed formulation, payroll and email to suppliers. Even small farms use a computer or smartphone for records, banking and market prices. This unit gives you the basic knowledge to use a computer confidently and safely.

Hardware and software

Hardware is the physical parts you can touch. Software is the programs that tell the hardware what to do.

PartJob
Processor (CPU)Does the calculations; the "brain"
Memory (RAM)Holds work while the computer is on; lost when switched off
Storage (hard drive or SSD)Keeps files and programs when switched off
Input devicesKeyboard, mouse, barcode scanner, touch screen
Output devicesMonitor, printer, till slip printer

Types of software

  • Operating system, such as Windows, macOS, Linux, Android: runs the computer and other programs.
  • Application software: word processor for letters, spreadsheet for stock and budgets, email, web browser, and business systems such as the store's point-of-sale or accounting package.

Networks and the internet

Computers in a store are usually connected in a network so the tills, the office and the warehouse share one stock system. The network connects to the internet through a router, using fibre, ADSL, wireless or a mobile data connection. In rural areas the connection can be slow or drop out, so many systems can work offline and update later.

Starting and shutting down

Switch on at the power button, wait for the operating system to load, and log in with your own username and password. Shut down using the operating system's shut-down option. Pulling the plug can damage files.

lessons.title: Working with files and programs
lessons.html:
Files and folders

A file is one piece of saved work: a letter, a stock list, a photo. A folder holds files, like a file cover in a filing cabinet. Organise folders logically, for example "Orders > 2026 > Fertiliser suppliers".

Good file habits

  • Give files clear names: "Stock count Feed store 2026-06-30" is better than "Doc1".
  • Save often while working; use Ctrl+S (or Command+S on a Mac).
  • Use "Save As" when you want a new copy with a different name.
  • Do not keep work files on the desktop only; use the folders or shared drive your business provides.
  • Delete files only when you are sure they are not needed. Deleted files usually go to the Recycle Bin first.

Basic program skills

  • Word processor: type, edit, format (bold, headings), check spelling, print.
  • Spreadsheet: enter data in cells and use simple formulas. In a stock sheet, if B2 has opening stock and C2 has sales, the formula =B2-C2 gives the balance.
  • Email: write a clear subject, attach files, check the address before sending.
  • Browser: find market prices, weather and supplier catalogues. Check that information comes from a reliable source.

Useful shortcuts

Keys (Windows)Action
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+VCopy / paste
Ctrl+ZUndo
Ctrl+PPrint
Alt+TabSwitch between programs

Printing

Choose the right printer, check the preview, and select only the pages you need. Paper and toner cost money.

lessons.title: Safe and healthy computer use
lessons.html:
Protecting information

Business computers hold customer accounts, prices and banking details. The Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA) requires businesses to protect personal information about customers and staff. You play a part.

  • Passwords: use a strong password (long, mixing words, numbers and symbols). Never share it or write it on a note stuck to the screen.
  • Lock the screen when you leave your desk (Windows key + L).
  • Phishing: be careful of emails asking you to click a link, open an attachment or change a supplier's bank details. Phone the supplier on a known number to check. Fraudsters often target agri businesses with fake "change of banking details" letters.
  • Viruses: do not plug in unknown flash drives or install software without permission. Keep antivirus software up to date.
  • Backups: important data must be backed up regularly, for example to the cloud or an external drive kept in another place. Ask who is responsible in your business.

Looking after the equipment

  • Keep food and drinks away from the keyboard.
  • Keep computers out of dust, direct sun and damp, which are common in grain stores and workshops.
  • Use surge protection; lightning and power surges damage equipment, especially in rural areas.
  • Report faults to IT instead of opening the computer yourself.

Your health

  • Sit with your back supported and feet flat; screen top at eye level.
  • Keep wrists straight when typing.
  • Look away from the screen every 20 minutes or so and take short breaks.
  • Do not overload plugs; trailing cables are a trip hazard.

Key points

  • Hardware is the physical parts; software is the programs.
  • Name and save files clearly in the right folders.
  • Never share passwords and lock your screen when away.
  • Check any request to change bank details by phone.
  • Back up important data and protect equipment from dust and power surges.
